item.title: Anthropic researcher says more than 10% chance AI "could kill all humans"
item.description:

item.title: OpenAI solution for the Navier-Stokes problem overshadowed by plagiarism controversy — researcher working on related proof claims his work with Codex influenced OpenAI's direction
Experts gather in Austin to explore how AI can improve disaster response and recovery
item.description:
AUSTIN (KXAN) — Artificial intelligence experts, emergency managers, researchers and technology leaders gathered in Austin on Wednesday for the [AIDE Summit](https://www.aideinitiative.org/summit-2026/), a conference focused on the growing role AI could play in disaster preparedness, response and recovery.
The event, hosted through the AI for Disasters and Emergencies (AIDE) Initiative, brought together stakeholders from across the country to discuss how artificial intelligence is already being used in emergency management and how communities can responsibly adopt new technologies in the future.
### Balancing Innovation and Public Safety Jessica Jensen, a [policy researcher with RAND](https://www.rand.org/about/people/j/jensen_jessica.html), said the term “artificial intelligence” is often misunderstood.

item.title: China ‘can never get ahead’ of US in AI, Bessent says in advance of Xi’s visit
item.description:
# China ‘can never get ahead’ of US in AI, Bessent says in advance of Xi’s visit ### Trump’s treasury secretary accuses Chinese artificial intelligence firms of ‘stealing and copying’, weeks before leadership summit in Washington US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent claimed that China “can never get ahead” of America in [artificial intelligence](https://www.scmp.com/topics/artificial-intelligence?module=inline&pgtype=article), in part due to its “central planning”, as three government agencies accused Beijing of maliciously copying technology from its leading firms.
The report claimed that the firms extracted “billions of tokens across millions of exchanges/requests from US frontier AI models, including variants of Claude, GPT, Gemini and Grok, since at least late 2024”.
